record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a localized time-dependent breather solution in higher spatial dimensions for a dispersive or hyperbolic wave equation? More concretely, can one construct such a higher-dimensional breather either through a nonlinear equation, a system of coupled equations, a suitable dispersion relation with spectral gaps, or even a linear problem with a time-dependent potential and a localized time-dependent spatial solution?

evidence.quote: Simply stated: Does there exist a breather solution in higher dimensions? The standard ”soliton resolution conjecture” says no. But of course, this can only be generically true.

The problem can be further simplified by asking for a linear problem with a time-dependent potential and a localized time-dependent spatial solution, in higher dimensions, see also Plum and Reichel (2022).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A breather is a smooth, spatially localized, time-periodic (or otherwise non-trivially time-dependent and non-decaying) solution of a wave-type equation. Classical examples in one spatial dimension include the breather of the sine–Gordon equation and certain breathers of the modified Korteweg–de Vries equation.

Construct, or prove the non-existence of, a higher-dimensional breather in the following sense. Let d ≥ 2. Find a function u : ℝ_t × ℝ^d_x → ℝ (or ℂ, or vector-valued) which:
(i) is smooth and globally defined in time,
(ii) is spatially localized (e.g. u(t, ·) ∈ L^2(ℝ^d) for every t, with sup_t ‖u(t,·)‖_{L^2(ℝ^d)} < ∞ and u(t,x) → 0 as |x| → ∞ uniformly in t),
(iii) is time-periodic, u(t+T, x) = u(t, x) for some T > 0, and is not stationary (not of the form e^{iωt}φ(x) reducible to a bound state), 
and which solves at least one of the following:
(a) a nonlinear dispersive or hyperbolic PDE on ℝ^d (e.g. a semilinear Klein–Gordon, nonlinear Schrödinger, or wave equation with a physically reasonable nonlinearity);
(b) a system of coupled dispersive/hyperbolic equations on ℝ^d;
(c) a linear dispersive equation on ℝ^d whose dispersion relation possesses suitable spectral gaps;
(d) a linear evolution equation i∂_t u = H(t) u (or a linear wave equation) on ℝ^d with a smooth, bounded, possibly time-dependent potential V(t,x), admitting a spatially localized, time-periodic, non-stationary solution.

Either exhibit such a u with explicit equation and verify (i)–(iii), or prove that no such u exists in the chosen class.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of constructing genuine higher-dimensional breathers for nonlinear dispersive/hyperbolic equations remains open and is widely regarded as such; the soliton resolution conjecture suggests generic non-existence. Partial constructions exist in special structured settings: Plum–Reichel and collaborators have constructed breathers for semilinear curl-curl wave equations with radially symmetric coefficients, and recent works (e.g. 2025 preprints on breather solutions for semilinear wave equations) continue to address the problem. Various (2+1)-dimensional integrable-type equations admit explicit "breather" solutions via Hirota/Darboux methods, but these are typically not localized in all spatial directions. No general resolution is known.

status_evidence.title: A Breather Construction for a Semilinear Curl-Curl Wave Equation with Radially Symmetric Coefficients
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of time-periodic spatially localized real-valued solutions (breathers) for a semilinear curl-curl wave equation with radially symmetric coefficients in 3D.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results in special higher-dimensional structured settings.

status_evidence.title: Breather solutions for semilinear wave equations (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study existence of breather solutions for semilinear wave equations.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Breathers and rogue waves for semilinear curl-curl wave equations
status_evidence.snippet: Continued investigations of breather solutions for curl-curl-type equations in higher dimensions.
